name: MAX_FIELD_GRAPHEMES
reason: 14,000 is a chosen display ceiling, not a bound. The block reason is a 227-char prefix at src/hooklib/stop-gate.ts:51-54, and the briefing itself has no finite upper bound since session entries render one line each with no count cap (src/domain/session-log.ts:12-18). 14,000 clears the 12,000-char render target at src/render/briefing.ts:17 plus that prefix, which is what an ordinary thread produces. A briefing over 14,000 is still silently truncated at hooks/lib/io.ts:49. This ceiling is also the only bound on the thread listing hooks/user-prompt-submit.ts:20 emits straight through from renderThreadListing (src/cli/session-start.ts:31-40), which has no count cap or clip of its own.

name: BANNER_MAX_GRAPHEMES
reason: Declared at src/cli/session-start.ts:12 rather than imported because src/ must not depend on hooks/; the equality with the hook transport was deliberately broken when the transport rose to 14000 to fit an ordinary briefing's block message, and the invariant that actually matters is preserved and strengthened, namely that the banner clips itself first through clipWithMarker so the transport truncation is a no-op and never removes the marker (docs/plans/2026-08-28-continuity-goal-model/U7-capture.md:633).

name: BRIEFING_MAX_CHARS
reason: Measured build-up of the worst case reaches about 10,600 characters and 12,000 is the smallest round ceiling with headroom (docs/specs/2026-08-26-briefing-scoping-repair.md:237-246,290-292); human-ruled, against the architect measurement that the prior spec 3,000 ceiling is unreachable at today caps. This ceiling is the target the clip search aims at, not a bound the reply always respects: a briefing that cannot fit even with every field rendered at its guaranteed minimum length is returned over this ceiling, and the page says so.

name: RESUME_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES
reason: The reply carries the briefing once, so this is BRIEFING_MAX_CHARS plus RESUME_PAYLOAD_RESERVE_BYTES plus the measured envelope of 26 thread-id bytes, 114 scaffold bytes and 78 previous-session bytes. It is the smallest ceiling at which a briefing sitting exactly on the character target always serialises, so bytes never bind plain ASCII and bind only content whose byte length exceeds its character length. This ceiling is the target the clip search aims at, not a bound the reply always respects: a briefing that cannot fit even with every field rendered at its guaranteed minimum length is returned over this ceiling, and the page says so.

name: RESUME_PAYLOAD_RESERVE_BYTES
reason: Target 12,218 bytes rather than 12,418 because the convergent search fills to whatever byte budget it is given, so budgeting at the raw cap would land content exactly on it, and a knife-edge equality is fragile against any later change; test/unit/briefing.test.ts:974 (briefing.the-clip-search-lands-just-under-the-byte-cap-on-the-worst-reachable-multi-byte-record) exercises the search converging against this target.

name: BRIEFING_COPIES_IN_RESUME_PAYLOAD
reason: The reply carries the briefing exactly once, in structuredContent.briefing; the text slot the resume_thread tool returns carries no copy of it.

name: SESSION_ENTRY_TEXT_FLOOR
reason: The guaranteed minimum for both shapes the session log renders: an older entry's first stored line, and the newest entry's block once it alone is too large to render whole. Chosen, not derived. It equals SESSION_FIRST_LINE_MAX at src/server/resource-render.ts:22, the limit the sessions resource already applies to the same quantity, so the two surfaces guarantee the same amount of a first line; that constant's own reason, 50 entries times 200 graphemes under the 12,000 briefing budget, does NOT carry over, because the briefing has no item cap and 145 entries are reachable. Measured on 2026-09-10 over the 145 entries of thread 01M24FHCMWGH0SHARH12CARCZ1: the escaped first line runs a median of 141 graphemes and 63.4 percent sit at or below 200. 500, the placeholder this replaces, leaves a projected 47,167-character page where 200 leaves 36,650; 80 sits below the median and cuts four headlines in five mid-clause. No value makes that thread fit, so none was chosen to try: the residue there is entry count, which decision B16 forbids addressing with a display-time item cap.

name: ARTIFACT_LABEL_FLOOR
reason: Equals ARTIFACT_LABEL_MAX, the write cap for this field, so a value stored at its maximum renders whole.

name: ARTIFACT_POINTER_FLOOR

name: HEADER_FIELD_ESCAPED_GRAPHEME_MAX
reason: The largest stored write cap among the six briefing header fields is 500: SPINE_ACTIVE_GOAL_MAX, SPINE_NEXT_STEP_MAX, SPINE_LAST_SESSION_MAX, SPINE_LANDED_MAX and THREAD_BLOCKED_BY_MAX in src/schema/caps.ts, while THREAD_TITLE_MAX is 200. This ceiling is measured after escaping, so what it guarantees is narrower than that write cap: a stored value whose escape is the identity renders whole even when it already sits at its write cap, and any value the escape expands past 500 is shortened here by design. The escape is not the identity on every plain-ASCII value, because escapeStored expands a markdown leading character at line start and always expands '<'; an all-ASCII 500-character value opening '- fix the parser' or containing 'a < b' measures 505 escaped and is shortened. No finite budget could avoid that, since 500 stored '<' characters escape to 3000 characters. The cap is therefore a different quantity from any one write cap rather than a copy of one, and it binds only once escaping expands a value past the largest of them.

name: CLIP_SEARCH_UPPER_BOUND
reason: The largest stored text any briefing field can hold, so no clip the search sets is ever capped below a value the store admits. It is no longer the top of the search itself: the search runs to CLIP_SEARCH_AXIS_UPPER_BOUND, which composes this ceiling with the per-item clip span. The thirteen per-field limits do not bound it, because a floor is a minimum and cannot bound a search from above.

name: CLIP_SEARCH_AXIS_LOWER_BOUND
reason: Equals SESSION_ENTRY_TEXT_FLOOR. The bottom of the clip search is every field at its floor, and the newest session entry is never shortened below what an older entry's headline is guaranteed, so the axis bottoms out at that floor rather than at MIN_TEXT_CLIP. Below it clipWithMarker returns the shortening marker alone (src/render/clip.ts:22-24), which would render the newest entry as a marker carrying none of its own text.

name: CLIP_SEARCH_AXIS_UPPER_BOUND
reason: The search runs one axis that composes two ranges so a single binary search expresses the render priority. At or below CLIP_SEARCH_UPPER_BOUND the axis point is the newest session entry's clip while every other field sits at its floor; above it the newest renders whole and the axis point drives every other field's clip from MIN_TEXT_CLIP up to CLIP_SEARCH_UPPER_BOUND. The top is therefore CLIP_SEARCH_UPPER_BOUND plus the per-item clip span, 32000 + (32000 - 14). Page size is non-decreasing along the axis, so the pass ceiling keeps its expression 1 + ceil(log2(range)) at test/unit/briefing.test.ts:846-847 and evaluates to 17 on this range, one render more than the 16 it evaluated to before.

name: SESSION_BODY_MAX
reason: Ruled by the human operator on 2026-09-09 (decision 01M24GFGJZEQE7JT4VJCRDBQS3). Across twenty-five entries, bodies ran a median of 2669 characters, largest 7814, against a cap of 8000; the largest is 98 percent of the ceiling, a sample censored by its own cap, so the observed maximum is a lower bound on demand rather than a measure of it. 32000 is four times the largest entry anyone has written.

name: THREAD_RECORD_SERIALISED_MAX_BYTES
reason: Largest live serialised thread record measured at 39,079 bytes (docs/plans/2026-08-28-continuity-goal-model/U1-schema-foundations.md:410-434), so the bound is 1.68x the largest record that exists; raising it was rejected as weakening a bound with no measured need, and anything below about 49,000 would be breached once U4 populated the new fields.

name: DECISION_RECORD_SERIALISED_MAX_BYTES
reason: A decision record and a thread record are both separately-stored records committed through the same store and therefore carry the same bound.

name: SESSION_FIRST_LINE_MAX
reason: 50 entries times this 200-grapheme limit is 10,000 graphemes of first-line text, under BRIEFING_MAX_CHARS of 12,000 (commit d83408ccd7af7836cc13abb57098df71c7f332f0).

name: SESSION_FIRST_LINE_ENTRIES_MAX
reason: 50 entries times the 200-grapheme SESSION_FIRST_LINE_MAX is 10,000 graphemes of first-line text, under BRIEFING_MAX_CHARS of 12,000 (commit d83408ccd7af7836cc13abb57098df71c7f332f0).
